decisions.reason: As a clear extension of the firm's established psychiatric and therapeutic services, it is likely to meet aspiration levels closely enough for an expanding organisation with some slack to continue backing it.

Although mission-linked through workshop activity, custom furniture is more peripheral to the core care business, so if results fall short of aspirations it could be reconsidered, but current expansion makes retention more likely than exit.
Outpatient sociotherapy is close to the firm's core support offer, so boundedly rational management would likely keep it while learning about demand rather than redeploy resources quickly.

Its home-page prominence suggests strategic importance and early internal confidence, and as a close fit with senior-care capabilities it is unlikely to fall below aspirations enough to be dropped soon.

The retail shop fits the sheltered-workshop mission but is less central than care services, so it faces somewhat higher review risk if performance is uncertain, though organisational slack still supports keeping it for now.
